subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` ACK require the user turn to be durably visible/progressing, or is the current UI-preserved optimistic message plus later runtime/fallback persistence the intended contract?
rationale: Current main mitigates stale-history UI replacement, but the remaining durable ACK/progress boundary affects session-state and message-delivery semantics and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Make ACK Durable
options.body: Require `chat.send` to ACK only after the user turn is durably visible or an explicit visible failure is available, likely by porting the useful part of the gateway candidate PR through the shared recorder boundary.

options.title: Keep Runtime-Owned Durability
options.body: Treat the current delayed runtime/fallback persistence model as intentional and close or narrow the issue after documenting what users should expect when dispatch stalls.

options.title: Review Existing Candidate PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80670 as design input, but require a current-main port before it can become the landing path.

recommendation.title: Make ACK Durable
recommendation.body: Require `chat.send` to ACK only after the user turn is durably visible or an explicit visible failure is available, likely by porting the useful part of the gateway candidate PR through the shared recorder boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question sits on the shared user-turn transcript recorder/session persistence boundary they appear to own by history.
